findings.reason: an implementer following §5 as written either fails its own ≤10 gate, or must edit a file outside the section's write scope, so the plan as authored sends the node into a scope-blocked or unsatisfiable gate.
findings.text: §5's mechanism unifies only `section_authored` (reckon/roadmap.py:184) and `readiness_state` (reckon/serve.py:2067) onto the `read_state_and_text` memo, but a cold roadmap read of a fresh project also parses every plan inside the metadata index build — `_plan_record` calls `_plan_html.read_state(text)` directly at reckon/metadata_index.py:593, and the index persists by content digest so a temporary project has no persisted entries to reuse. Plus `read_state_file` (memo kind `read_state`) is reachable on the roadmap path via `_plan_followups` (reckon/roadmap.py:1337). If only the named readers are unified, a cold roadmap read alone yields two parses per plan (index + section_authored) = twenty for ten plans, already above the asserted bound of ten before the discovery read is counted — and reaching ten would require editing `reckon/metadata_index.py`, which is not among §5's declared write paths (`reckon/roadmap.py`, `reckon/serve.py`, the test).
